issues.description: The problem statement (and the template) specify Developer.attend(course:) should take an optional Course? parameter, but the solution implements attend(course:) with a non-optional Course parameter. This divergence is structural (method signature differs) and can confuse students and tests that expect the method to accept nil and use optional binding.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's attend(course:) signature match the specification and template by accepting an optional Course? parameter and using optional binding inside the method. Alternatively, if the intent is to require a non-optional Course, update the problem statement and template to specify Course (non-optional). The preferred fix is to update the solution to func attend(course: Course?) { ... } and handle nil cases as described in the problem.

issues.description: The attend(course:) API is inconsistent between artifacts: the problem statement and the template require an optional parameter (Course?), but the solution implements attend(course:) with a non-optional Course parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (optional vs. non-optional parameter) breaks the conceptual mapping for students who are asked to use optional binding on the course parameter and may cause confusion about the expected implementation and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attend(course:) signature consistent across all artifacts. Prefer matching the problem statement: change the solution implementation to accept an optional Course (func attend(course: Course?)) and use optional binding inside the method as described, or alternatively update the problem statement and template to expect a non-optional Course if that was the intended design.
